note: Pixlate's Of Manors & Mayhem, as written in the author's Bloodstar almanac. The 24 characters above the almanac's "Slop Alert" marker are published; the 10 below it, which that marker calls unfinished, are drafts. Slop Alert itself is not a playable character and is not imported. Xanadu's two extra tokens (the good and evil unlisted-character tokens, xanadu1_omnm / xanadu2_omnm) are folded into the one Xanadu page: the evil token is its alt art and a side box records both.

collection.author: Pixlate
collection.synopsis: In the gilded halls of Ravenswood Manor, socialites mix with elites across the Bluff whilst the hoi polloi look upwards to see an endless golden reprieve from a life of squalor. No troubles echo through these finely decorated halls. But on one night, when the stars draw a perfect arc across the midnight sky as the masquerade continues its fifth song, a celestial force can be felt throughout the ballrooms of the Manor as unearthly presences begin their descent. These evils do not hail from the fiery pits beneath, but are abstract, heavenly, and as witnesses to their glory have described it, beautiful. And for the first time, the gentry of Ravenswood Bluff feel a trembling upon their skin the commonfolk know all too well. For whilst walls and hedgerows may insulate you from ordinary dangers, something will always disrupt the best-laid plans...

customBoxes.title: Credits
customBoxes.content:
Of Manors & Mayhem is a homebrew character collection by Pixlate for Blood on the Clocktower by the Pandemonium Institute.

- Character art and almanac text by Pixlate.
- Imported from the author's Bloodstar almanac: https://bloodstar.clocktica.com/p/Pixlate/OMnM/almanac.html

characters.name: Carpenter
characters.ability: Each night, choose a player: you learn if they are a Townsfolk or a Demon.
characters.lede: The Carpenter learns who are Townsfolk, but can't tell them apart from the Demon.
howToRun: Each night, wake the Carpenter and prompt them to choose a player. If they are a Townsfolk or a Demon, nod your head to indicate a "Yes." Otherwise, shake your head to indicate a "No." Put the Carpenter back to sleep.
examples: The Carpenter chooses the Savant and learns a "Yes". On the next night, the Carpenter chooses the No Dashii and learns a "Yes".
The Carpenter chooses the Butler and learns a "No". On the next night, the Carpenter chooses the Fearmonger and learns a "No".
characters.quote: How can you say to your brother, ‘Brother, let me take the speck out of your eye,’ when you yourself fail to see the plank in your own eye? You hypocrite, first take the plank out of your eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.
characters.flavor: How can you say to your brother, ‘Brother, let me take the speck out of your eye,’ when you yourself fail to see the plank in your own eye? You hypocrite, first take the plank out of your eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.
characters.creator: Pixlate

characters.name: Clerk
characters.ability: Each night, choose 2 players (not yourself): you learn whose character is later in the script order.
characters.lede: The Clerk compares players' position on the script.
summaryBullets: Each night, the Clerk chooses 2 players, and learns which player appears later in the script order. Script order by default goes Townsfolk, Outsider, Minion, Demon. On a 1-column script, script order is obvious (top-to-bottom) but in 2-column, be sure to establish which column goes first (typically, it is down the first column, then down the second). If the Clerk picks two players with the same character, shake your head to indicate that neither of them come later than the other in the script order.
howToRun: Each night, wake the Clerk and prompt them to choose 2 players - point to the player whose character appears later in the script order (if they are the same character, shake your head "No"). Put the Clerk back to sleep.
examples: The Clerk chooses the Poisoner and the Imp. The Clerk is pointed at the Imp.
The Clerk chooses the Alchemist and the Drunk Chef. The Clerk learns the Drunk Chef.
The Clerk chooses the Farmer and the player who just became another Farmer. The Storyteller shakes their head, and puts the Clerk back to sleep.
characters.quote: Hello, Mr. Morozov, let me just bring up your documents... hmmm, you should be between Mr. Minstrel and Ms. Nightwatchman, but I'm afraid there's no file present. Let me check again before I call my supervisor.
characters.flavor: Hello, Mr. Morozov, let me just bring up your documents... hmmm, you should be between Mr. Minstrel and Ms. Nightwatchman, but I'm afraid there's no file present. Let me check again before I call my supervisor.
characters.creator: Pixlate

characters.name: Janitor
characters.ability: Each night, you learn 2 players: the 2nd neighbors a non-Townsfolk if (& only if) the 1st is a Townsfolk.
characters.lede: The Janitor learns which players neighbor troublemakers.
summaryBullets: If the first player the Janitor learns is a Townsfolk, the second player must neighbor at least one player who isn't a Townsfolk. This includes dead neighbors. If the first player the Janitor learns is not a Townsfolk, the second player must neighbor 2 Townsfolk. The Janitor may learn themselves.
howToRun: Each night, place the FIRST reminder token next to a player. If that player is a Townsfolk, place the SECOND reminder token next to a player who neighbors a non-Townsfolk player (Minion, Demon or Outsider). If that player is not a Townsfolk, place the SECOND reminder token on a player who neighbors 2 Townsfolk.
examples: The Leviathan neighbors the Marionette. On the first night, the Janitor learns the Savant and the Marionette.
The Janitor neighbors the Drunk and the Scarlet Woman. They are woken to learn the Vortox and themselves.
characters.quote: Oh dear. Look at the mess. No doubt some troublemaker's causing a ruckus in the quadrangle again. In a respectable establishment such as this one? To think of it! And right next to where I had to mop up the bloodstains yesterday.
characters.flavor: Oh dear. Look at the mess. No doubt some troublemaker's causing a ruckus in the quadrangle again. In a respectable establishment such as this one? To think of it! And right next to where I had to mop up the bloodstains yesterday.
characters.creator: Pixlate
characters.firstNightReminder: Wake the Janitor and point to 2 players.
characters.otherNightReminder: Wake the Janitor and point to 2 players.

characters.name: Surgeon
characters.ability: Each night*, you learn a dead character.
characters.lede: The Surgeon learns which characters are dead.
characters.quote: Note #133: Patient arrived dead on site with large lacerations across upper abdominal and severe bleeding. Cause of death unknown but likely related to large pitchfork found protruding from patient's chest. More testing required.
characters.flavor: Note #133: Patient arrived dead on site with large lacerations across upper abdominal and severe bleeding. Cause of death unknown but likely related to large pitchfork found protruding from patient's chest. More testing required.
characters.creator: Pixlate

characters.name: Pawnbroker
characters.ability: Each day, you may visit the Storyteller to answer a numerical question: you learn if you're correct.
characters.lede: The Pawnbroker makes guesses, and learns if they're correct.
summaryBullets: Each day, the Pawnbroker may approach the Storyteller to learn a question whose answer is a number, after which the Pawnbroker may guess a number. They learn if their answer was higher or lower than the correct value, or if they guessed exactly right. The question may be anything as long as it can be answered using a number. The Storyteller should aim to make the questions not trivially answered, but also not impossibly obtuse. Remember that the Pawnbroker still learns useful information if they get it wrong.
howToRun: Each day, when the Pawnbroker approaches you for their question, give a question which can be answered by a number. If the Pawnbroker answeres correctly, indicate a "Yes" in some way. If the Pawnbroker is wrong, indicate a "No" in some way.
examples: On the 1st day, the Storyteller asks the Pawnbroker "How many pairs of evil players are sitting next to each other?" The Pawnbroker guesses 1 and the Storyteller shakes their head. On the 2nd day, the Storyteller asks the Pawnbroker "How many Townsfolk are seated on the couch?" The Pawnbroker guesses 2 and the Storyteller nods their head.
characters.quote: You think I'm giving you 500 for that lousy old trident thing you've got? No buyer is looking for oversized red Halloween decorations in the middle of March. My friend, I'll give you 40 and a firm handshake and we can call it a deal. Shake on it.
characters.flavor: You think I'm giving you 500 for that lousy old trident thing you've got? No buyer is looking for oversized red Halloween decorations in the middle of March. My friend, I'll give you 40 and a firm handshake and we can call it a deal. Shake on it.
characters.creator: Pixlate

characters.name: Orator
characters.ability: Each day, visit the Storyteller & make a (non-ambiguous) statement: they reply with something equally true.
characters.lede: The Orator enters a dialogue with the Storyteller to discover what is and isn't true.
summaryBullets: Each day, the Orator privately visits the Storyteller to make a statement with a clear 'true' or 'false' evaluation. If the Storyteller deems that the Orator's statement is too ambiguous, the Storyteller may ask the Orator to try again, or to come back with a non-ambiguous statement. Depending on the script, the Storyteller may optionally run that the Orator may make ambiguous statements involving subjective opinion, and that the Storyteller may respond with something equally subjectively true. Do this at your own caution! If the Orator says something they know to be objectively true, give them something much less helpful. Correspondingly, if the Orator takes a risk by being very specific, be equally specific in return - reward them!
howToRun: Each day, when the Orator makes a statement to you, reply with something true (if it was true) or false (if it was false).
examples: Jamie the Orator visits the Storyteller on the first day and says that "The Demon neighbors an Outsider." The Storyteller responds with "The Drunk neighbors a Minion." Both statements are false.

Pierre the Orator visits the Storyteller on the 3rd day and says "2 + 2 = 4." The Storyteller responds with "4 + 4 = 8." Later, Pierre says that "The good team is winning," and the Storyteller asks him to try again. Pierre gets what he deserves.
The Orator says "I neighbor exactly 1 evil player." The Storyteller says "There is a Vigormortis in play," which is false because the Orator neighbors the Barber and the Vortox.
The Orator is receiving reversed info. They visit the Storyteller to say "There is a King in play," which is false, and learn "There is a Marionette in play," which is true.
tips: When running Orator, try your best to mirror the strength and specificity of the Orator's statement. If the Orator is attempting to make an axiomatically true or false statement, such as "I am the Orator," and knowing the polarity of the information being received is important, consider telling them something vague, less helpful, or something very difficult to accurately determine the truthfulness of.
characters.quote: Reality is exactly what you call it. I speak, and the universe listens.
characters.flavor: Reality is exactly what you call it. I speak, and the universe listens.
characters.creator: Pixlate

characters.name: Priest
characters.ability: Outsiders start knowing you are the Priest. [-1 to +? Outsiders]
characters.lede: The Priest offers guidance to Outsiders.
summaryBullets: During setup, the Priest either removes an Outsider or adds any number of Outsiders to the bag. At the start of the game, all Outsiders learn who the Priest is. If a Priest is created mid-game, all Outsiders who the Priest is that night.
howToRun: While setting up the game, before putting character tokens in the bag, either remove one Outsider token & add one Townsfolk token, or remove any number of Townsfolk tokens & add any number of Outsider tokens.
On the first night, wake any Outsider. Show them the Priest token, then point to the Priest player. Put them to sleep. Repeat until all Outsiders have been woken.
examples: AP is the Priest. On the first night of an 8-player game, the Puzzlemaster and Mutant both learn that AP is the Priest. Despite the base Outsider count being 1, there are 2 Outsiders in play, because AP has added an Outsider to the game.
The Priest is in-play in a 12-player game. Only 1 Outsider, the Heretic, is in play, due to the Priest’s ability. On the first night, the Heretic learns who the Priest is.

The Pit-Hag turns Basil, the starting Witch, into the Priest. That night, all Outsiders learn Basil is the Priest. The next night, the Pit-Hag turns Iris into the Mutant. Iris learns who the Priest is.
characters.quote: Speak thy Shibboleth, and all who do shall be welcomed with open arms to the land of plenty.
characters.flavor: Speak thy Shibboleth, and all who do shall be welcomed with open arms to the land of plenty.
characters.creator: Pixlate

characters.name: Croupier
characters.ability: If a Minion nominates, executes, & kills the Demon (ending the game), they change alignment, even if you are dead.
characters.lede: The Croupier allows a Minion to risk it all in order to win with good.
summaryBullets: If a Minion nominates, executes, and kills the Demon, resulting in the end of the game, the Minion switches alignments. A good Minion becomes evil, and an evil Minion becomes good. This happens before win conditions are evaluated.
howToRun: If a Minion nominates, executes and kills their Demon, and this kill leads to the end of the game, turn their token upside down to signify that they are now a good Minion.
examples: The Croupier is in play. On day 4, the Croupier publicly comes out and asks any Minions if they would like to out their Demon and win with good. The Wizard nominates, executes and kills the No Dashii. The Wizard turns good, and good wins.
The Croupier is not in play. Jack, the Choirboy, is bluffing Croupier. When he comes out, Eliza the Baron believes him and executes his own Demon. Eliza loses with the evil team.
The Poisoner nominates and executes the Demon. Although there is a Croupier in play, they do not turn good because the game has continued thanks to the Scarlet Woman.
A good Minion is in play (for some reason). They nominate, execute and kill the Vortox, thinking there is a Heretic in play, but there is not. They turn evil, and good wins.
characters.quote: Ladies and gentlemen, all bets are off. All on black I see Mister... hm, I'm sorry, I don't think I've seen you here before. Thank you very much for choosing to sit at our table today, I wish you the best of luck.
characters.flavor: Ladies and gentlemen, all bets are off. All on black I see Mister... hm, I'm sorry, I don't think I've seen you here before. Thank you very much for choosing to sit at our table today, I wish you the best of luck.
characters.creator: Pixlate

characters.name: Boxer
characters.ability: Minions you nominate die. If you nominate a good player, you are drunk.
characters.lede: The Boxer punches Minions.
summaryBullets: If the Boxer nominates a Minion, the Minion immediately dies. If the Boxer nominates a good player, the Boxer is immediately and drunk until the Boxer ability leaves play. The Boxer may nominate several Minions in one game, and kill multiple Minions in one game. Calling for exiles does not make the Boxer drunk, even if the Traveller was good.
howToRun: If the Boxer nominates a Minion, immediately declare that they are dead (do not explain why). If the Boxer nominates a good player, place the DRUNK reminder token on the Boxer.
examples: Mark is the Boxer. On the first day, he nominates the Scarlet Woman, who dies. The next day, he nominates the good Tea Lady. The day after, he nominates the Poisoner, who does not die.
Zaky is the Boxer. On the first day, he nominates the Imp, who is evil. He does nominate further until the fifth day, when he nominates the Baron, who dies.
characters.quote: I didn't hear no bell.
characters.flavor: I didn't hear no bell.
characters.creator: Pixlate

characters.name: Skunk
characters.ability: When you die, your good neighbors might die at any point from now on.
characters.lede: The Skunk’s death might spread to its good neighbors.
summaryBullets: The Skunk’s closest clockwise and anticlockwise good neighbors are affected when the Skunk dies, regardless of whether they are alive or dead. Neighboring evil players are skipped. The affected good players might die during the day or during the night. They might also not die at all. If the Skunk dies while drunk or poisoned, their good neighbors can’t die to the Skunk ability.
howToRun: If the Skunk is dead, you may decide at any point from then on that one (or both) of the Skunk’s good neighbors die. If this is during the day, immediately declare that they have died. If this is during the night, mark them with one of the Skunk’s DEAD reminder tokens and wait until dawn to declare which players died during the night. (Do not say how.)
examples: Dusk the dead Skunk neighbors Axolator, the Gambler, and nothership, the Carpenter. Axolator gambles Dusk as the Skunk, but dies anyway. When nothership nominates the next day, he dies. Both of them died to the Skunk ability.

Clockwise from the Skunk sits the Godfather, the evil Bishop, and the Soldier. Anticlockwise from the Skunk sits the Recluse, then the Courtier. When the Skunk dies, the Soldier and Courtier both die to the Skunk ability.

The Skunk dies. In the night, the Innkeeper protects the good neighbors of the Skunk, and the Storyteller cannot kill them with the Skunk ability, since the Innkeeper is protecting them. Later that night, the Innkeeper dies. The Storyteller can now choose to kill one or both of the Skunk’s good neighbors, and does so.
characters.quote: You know what they say about he who smelt it...
characters.flavor: You know what they say about he who smelt it...
characters.creator: Pixlate

characters.name: Mystic
characters.ability: Minions who die after you do keep their ability.
characters.lede: The Mystic communes with evil spirits.
summaryBullets: When the Mystic dies, any Minions who die from that point on will keep their ability, and wake for their ability. The Minions are still dead, they just retain their ability. If a Minion is dead, and the Mystic dies, that Minion does not regain their ability. If the Mystic is drunk or poisoned when it dies, any Minions who subsequently die will not keep their abilities. - If the Mystic is dead, and is then drunk or poisoned, Minions who have their ability due to the Mystic's ability will lose their ability, and will regain them when the Mystic regains their ability. The same applies if the Mystic ability otherwise ceases to be in play. If a dead Minion who has their ability due to the Mystic changes character into another Minion, they keep their new Minion ability.
howToRun: When the Mystic dies, from that point onwards, mark any Minions who die with the HAS ABILITY reminder token. That Minion has their ability, and wakes for that ability as per usual.
examples: Jack the Mystic is executed. That night, Vivian the Imp kills the Assassin, and Jacob the Assassin kills the Mayor, despite being dead.
The Poisoner is dead. The Mystic is killed that night, but the Poisoner does not regain their ability. That day, the Witch dies after cursing themselves, but keeps their ability.
characters.quote: Truth is not a solid thing, there nothing at which to point the suggestion of an abstract understanding. Wisdom and magick are but two equally ethereal sides of the same coin.
characters.flavor: Truth is not a solid thing, there nothing at which to point the suggestion of an abstract understanding. Wisdom and magick are but two equally ethereal sides of the same coin.
characters.creator: Pixlate

characters.name: Fae
characters.ability: Each night*, if you were mad as a Townsfolk today, you might become it. [+? Fae]
characters.lede: The Fae trick the town together.
summaryBullets: When setting up the bag, replace any number of Outsiders or Townsfolk with Fae tokens. If a Fae player was mad they were a Townsfolk today, they might become the Townsfolk they were mad as. This can duplicate in play Townsfolk. Generally speaking, the stronger the ability, the more convincing the Fae should be and the longer they might need to be mad for. Additionally, the more Fae there are in the bag, the more readily they should turn into the Townsfolk they were mad as. A dead Fae cannot change characters due to their ability.
howToRun: Each night after the first, you may wake a Fae player. Show them the YOU ARE info card, and then the token of the Townsfolk they become. Put the Fae to sleep.
examples: Nathan is the Fae. For two days, he is claiming Shugenja with an anti-clockwise. After 2 executions, he becomes the Shugenja and learns clockwise. Oops.

It is a 12 player game. Alex, Benjamin, Charlie, Dmitri, Emily, Fatima, George and Holly are all Fae. On the 1st day, Alex is mad as the Washerwoman, Benjamin and Charlie are mad as the Savant, Dmitri is mad as the Ravenkeeper, Emily is mad as the Empath, Fatima is mad as the Lycanthrope, George is mad as the Philosopher, and Holly is mad as the Alchemist. That night, Charlie becomes the Savant, Dmitri becomes the Ravenkeeper and Holly becomes the Alchemist.
It is a 10 player game. The Balloonist has added a Fae, which has added 3 more Fae. There are 4 Fae in total.
It is a 9 player game. There is 1 Fae and 1 Heretic. The Fae is mad as the Noble for 2 days, and becomes the Noble on the 3rd night.
tips: Storytellers have incredible discretion as to when and which Fae become Townsfolk. Keep balance in mind, with the understanding that the Fae should be wilfully propogating fabricated information, and both the proportion of Fae to other Townsfolk, and the relative strengths of the potential abilities.
characters.quote: Oft fire is without smoke, / And perill without show.
characters.flavor: Oft fire is without smoke, / And perill without show.
characters.creator: Pixlate

characters.name: Vigilante
characters.ability: The 1st time an evil player dies, they don't.
characters.lede: The Vigilante protects the other side.
characters.quote: Don't worry, I'm here to save you!
characters.flavor: Don't worry, I'm here to save you!
characters.creator: Pixlate

characters.name: Rogue
characters.ability: 1 good player is drunk. Each night*, guess who: if correct, you die.
characters.lede: The Rogue can do things the easy way or the hard way.
characters.quote: If you think this is bad, you should've seen the other guy.
characters.flavor: If you think this is bad, you should've seen the other guy.
characters.creator: Pixlate

characters.name: Gambit
characters.ability: Once per game, while dead & before nominations, publicly choose a player: they win if (& only if) you do.
characters.lede: The Gambit makes players win with them.
summaryBullets: If the Gambit is dead, and nominations have not been opened, they can publicly choose a player. That player wins only if the Gambit wins. This does not change that player's alignment. They are not informed that they win with the Gambit. Any dead player may claim Gambit.
howToRun: Once a Gambit claim has been made from a dead Gambit, place the CAPTURED reminder token on the chosen player. They now only win if the Gambit wins. They do not change alignments.
examples: There is a Croupier in play and the Goblin is looking to betray the Demon. Today, before nominations, the Gambit claims to be Gambit and chooses the Goblin. The Goblin nominates and executes the Demon. Good wins, and the Goblin, despite being good, loses with the Gambit.

There is no Gambit in play. Josh the Xaan claims Gambit and chooses the Heretic. The Heretic publicly claims to be the Heretic, and the Demon kills themselves. Evil wins and the Heretic loses with good.
characters.quote: Heavy is the hand that crowns the head.
characters.flavor: Heavy is the hand that crowns the head.
characters.creator: Pixlate

characters.name: Sidewinder
characters.ability: On your 1st night, choose a direction: Townsfolk between you & the Demon in that direction receive reversed info.
characters.lede: The Sidewinder reverses all info between them and the Demon.
summaryBullets: The Sidewinder wakes on the first night to reverse a portion of Townsfolk's information. Reversed info is true if it would be false, and false if it would be true. If there are multiple Demons, only information in the chosen direction between the Sidewinder and the closest Demon in that direction are reversed.
howToRun: On the first night, wake the Sidewinder and prompt them to point in a direction. Place either the CLOCKWISE or COUNTERCLOCKWISE token on the Sidewinder. Put them to sleep. Whilst they live, all info between them and the Demon in that direction is reversed.
examples: On the 1st night, the Sidewinder chooses clockwise. Sitting between them and the Demon in that direction are the Savant, Noble, Steward, and Gossip. The Noble learns 3 good players. The Steward learns an evil player. The Gossip is unaffected because it does not learn info. The Savant is unaffected, because the reverse of a true and a false statement is a false and a true statement.
characters.quote: In the cold and ssilent night, torchlight and candlewick can give no ssolace againsst the quiet encroach of sshadow everlassting.
characters.flavor: In the cold and ssilent night, torchlight and candlewick can give no ssolace againsst the quiet encroach of sshadow everlassting.
characters.creator: Pixlate
characters.firstNightReminder: Wake the Sidewinder & prompt them for a direction.

characters.name: Camarillo
characters.ability: The 1st time the Demon dies at night, they don't & register as dead, waking every 2nd night.
characters.lede: The Camarillo keeps things going, long after their Demon is dead.
summaryBullets: The 1st time the Demon dies at night, they don't die, but the Storyteller acts as if they died. Deaths are announced as normal. A living Demon which registers as dead obeys all the rules pertaining to dead players, the only difference being that they are secretly still alive. The game continues if there is a "dead" Demon and two living players. If the Camarillo dies, is drunk, or is poisoned, the Demon stops waking. The Demon still retains all secondary Demon abilities whilst they falsely register as dead. If the Demon dies whilst they register as dead due to the Camarillo, they die for real.
howToRun: The 1st time the Demon player dies at night, place the ONCE reminder token beside the Camarillo, and place WAKES TONIGHT token next to the Demon player. For each successive night, turn the WAKES TONIGHT token upside down to indicate when the Demon would not wake, and right side up to indicate when the Demon would wake.
examples: At night, the Vortox kills themselves. They live, but register as dead. The next night, the Vortox does not wake, but the Oracle falsely learns there are 0 dead evil players because the Vortox still has their ability. The next night, the Vortox wakes and kills the Flowergirl.
The Po dies at night. That day, the Po is executed whilst registering as dead. The Po dies and good wins.
The Sailor makes the Camarillo drunk. That night, the Demon does not wake, even though they should have. The next night, the Demon still does not wake, because they should have woken last night.
characters.quote: Sangre por sangria, mi amor.
characters.flavor: Sangre por sangria, mi amor.
characters.creator: Pixlate

characters.name: Czar
characters.ability: Players can't nominate & may point to vote for who is executed at dusk, even if you are dead.
characters.lede: The Czar makes all voting happen at once.
summaryBullets: If the Czar is in play, the Storyteller does not declare that nominations are open. If a player tries to nominate, tell them that they cannot nominate. They may talk and communicate as normal, they just can't nominate. This happens even if the Czar is dead. Just before putting the players to sleep, declare that Czar voting will commence. All players now have an opportunity to point at a player (choose an appropriate countdown). After the voting phase has ended, tell your players to not move from where they are currently pointing. If a player has enough votes as per the standard vote threshold (half of all living players, rounded up), that player is immediately executed - declare who has been executed as per normal. If a dead player points at someone during Czar voting, they spend their vote token as per usual. If a player is not pointing at anyone, they don't vote. If it is ambiguous who someone is pointing at, feel free to ask them who they intend to be pointing at.
howToRun: If the Czar is in play, do not announce that nominations have opened. If a player tries to nominate, inform them that they cannot. After running through the day, before telling the players to close their eyes, announce that the Czar is collecting votes and give a short countdown to allow players to point at who they wish to vote. If a player has enough votes to beat the minimum requirement, the player with the most votes is executed. Collect any spent vote tokens as normal.
examples: Joseph is the Czar. There are 9 players alive. When players sit back down after having private conversations, the Storyteller allows them to discuss as per usual. Billy nominates Dani, but is told he cannot. The Storyteller counts down towards the end of the day, at which point they announce that the Czar will be collecting votes. After a short countdown, 3 players are pointing at Joseph, 4 are pointing at Dani, and 2 players do not have their hands up. Nobody is executed, and the night begins.

There are 5 alive players and 3 dead players. After the Czar voting occurs, 2 dead players and 2 alive players are pointing at Nikola the Czar. 1 dead player is pointing at the Savant. Everyone else is not pointing at anybody. Nikola is executed, and all dead players lose their deadvotes.
The Courtier chooses the Czar. That day, nominations happen as usual. When the Courtier dies, the Czar's ability prevents people from nominating that day.
tips: Understand that since there will be no nominations and only one round of voting, keep the period of time after players return to their seats shorter than usual. Additionally, whilst you don't want to be giving players too much time to plan out votes to respect the Czar's ability, try to afford more time on the final day to keep things climactic. Use your own best judgement!
characters.quote: The ignorance of the many gives way for the tyranny of the few.
characters.flavor: The ignorance of the many gives way for the tyranny of the few.
characters.creator: Pixlate

characters.name: Katastroph
characters.ability: On night 2, choose 1 good player to learn who you are, & 2 players to learn falsely. After day 2, evil wins.
characters.lede: The Katastroph brings about the apocalypse on day 2.
summaryBullets: On night 2, the Katastroph will wake to choose 1 good player to learn who the Katastroph is. They will also choose 2 other players who will learn a player who is not the Katastroph. Only the player who learns who the Katastroph is must be good, the other two players can be evil. After day 2, if the Katastroph lives, evil immediately wins.
howToRun: On the first day, mark the Katastroph with the DAY 1 reminder. At the beginning of each following day, mark the Katastroph with the DAY 2 reminder. If a day ends and the Katastroph has the DAY 2 reminder token on them, declare that evil wins.

If it is the night after the DAY 1 reminder was placed down, wake the Katastroph and prompt them to pick 1 good player, and 2 other players of any alignement. Put the Katastroph to sleep. Wake the 1 good player, show them the THIS PLAYER IS, point to the Katastroph, and show them the Katastroph token. Do the same for the other 2 players, but point to a player who is NOT the Katastroph.
examples: Amy is the Katastroph. She choose that Bill the Savant learns who she is, and for Marcus the Poisoner and Andre the Steward to learn falsely. That night, Bill is woken to learn Amy, Marcus is woken to learn Bill and Andre is woken to learn Tyler.

It is day 2, and the Katastroph has chosen the Artist to learn who they are, and for the Oracle and the Village Idiot to learn falsely. In addition to this, the Xaan and the Spy also come out and say that they have also learnt that other players are the Katastroph.
tips: Don't always wake the player who correctly learns the name of the Katastroph first, in order to avoid players predicting who got the correct name based on the order in which they woke up.
characters.quote: Through me you go into a city of weeping; through me you go into eternal pain; through me you go amongst the lost people.

characters.name: Hororkka
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. Townsfolk who nominate are poisoned. [-1 Outsider]
characters.lede: The Hororkka poisons nominators.
summaryBullets: During set-up, if a Hororkka is in the bag, replace one Outsider with a Townsfolk. If Townsfolk nominates, from that point on, as long as the Hororkka lives, they are poisoned. This poisoning does not go away. If the Hororkka ability ceases to be in play, the poisoning stops.
howToRun: During nominations, if a player who nominates is a Townsfolk, mark them with the POISONED reminder. That player is poisoned until the Hororrka dies or leaves play.
Each night (except the first), wake the Hororkka and prompt them to point to a player. That player dies - mark them with the DEAD reminder token. Put the Hororkka back to sleep.
examples: The Hororkka is in play. The Town Crier nominates and receives false info the following night. The Tea Lady nominates their neighbor, who is no longer protected because the Tea Lady is poisoned. The Heretic nominates and remains sober.

Jackie is the Wraith bluffing as the Klutz. She wants to be the only nomination, and argues that people should not nominate in case of a Hororkka. However, Bobbie the Washerwoman is willing to nominate too. That night, Jackie directs the Hororkka to kill Bobbie. The next day, Jackie is able to direct an execution.

characters.name: Fabularum
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. Evil players may call for & look inside the Grimoire at any time.
characters.lede: The Fabularum has the Storyteller at their beck and call.
summaryBullets: All evil players know that they have the ability to call for & look inside the Grimoire at any time. This includes during the day, during nominations, and when they wake up at night. If an evil player wishes to look at the Grimoire (either surreptitiously or publicly), they may request to see it. If a Fabularum enters play, all evil players learn that they have gained the ability to call for and look at the Grimoire. If a Fabularum leaves play, evil players should be informed that they no longer have this ability as to prevent cheating.
howToRun: At the earliest opportunity, inform all evil players that a Fabularum is in play and that they may call for and look at the Grimoire at any time. If, during the night or day, an evil player calls for the Grimoire, either bring it to them or allow them to get up and look at it. Each night (not the first), wake the Fabularum to choose a player to kill. Mark that player with the DEAD reminder token and announce their death in the morning.
examples: Damien is the Fabularum. On the 1st night, as he is recieving his Demon bluffs, he points to the Grimoire and gestures for the Storyteller to bring it so that he can look inside. That same night, Michael and Brittany are woken to learn each other and their Demon. They learn they can call for the Grimoire and stand up to peer inside before making their choices.
Alex is the Psychopath. Before nominations, he declares "Storyteller, bring me my Grimoire!" Scott the Storyteller sheepishly carries over the Grimoire to Alex before Alex kills Vivian, the Banshee.
Matt is the Poisoner bluffing Savant. As he approaches the Storyteller to pretend he is learning his info, he leans over to peek into the Grimoire to craft his information.

characters.name: Steeplechase
characters.ability: Nominators must 'tag' their nominees before you count down from 10, or the nomination immediately fails.
characters.lede: The Steeplechase gives players a run for their money.
summaryBullets: The Steeplechase may count down as slow or as fast as they want. The Steeplechase may choose to not count down at all. If the nominator does not 'tag' their nominee, the nomination fails, and votes are not tallied.
howToRun: During nominations, after the nomination is stated, prompt the Steeplechase to begin counting down. They may count down as slow or as fast as they wish. If the nominator does not tag their nominee, their nomination fails.
examples: Chris, the good Steeplechase travels in. Sarah nominates Edward and the Steeplechase steadily starts counting down from 10. Sarah tags Edward and the nomination goes through as normal.

The evil Steeplechase travels in. Ali nominates Stephen. The Steeplechase immediately rushes to count down from 10 and Ali barely has any time. Stephen cannot be nominated again, and votes are not tallied.
Aiden has broken his leg and is playing from a wheelchair. When Adam travels in as the Steeplechase, the Storyteller announces that a 'tag' will be defined as winning a thumb war.
tips: Before adding a Steeplechase, ask for the players' consent. If running or mobility is an issue, consider running something other than "tag" as the chase, for example, winning a thumb war, or speed typing a sentence within the time limit. Get creative!

characters.name: Xanadu
characters.ability: There might be 1 unlisted Minion & Townsfolk in play. They start knowing each other's characters.
characters.lede: Xanadu brings in characters from beyond the script.
summaryBullets: During set-up, the Storyteller might replace 1 Minion and 1 Townsfolk with 2 blank tokens or 2 Xanadu tokens (1 good and 1 evil). On the 1st night, players who draw the Xanadu tokens are woken up to learn which Townsfolk and Minion they are respectively. They also learn which other unlisted character is in play. This information must be true, even if they are drunk or poisoned. Xanadu does not need to add in 2 unlisted characters. If the characters added in by Xanadu have a setup effect, the setup effect applies.
howToRun: On the 1st night, wake the 2 players with an unlisted character & inform them of which other unlisted character is in play. Run their abilities accordingly, using the ? tokens, if necessary.
examples: Xanadu is in play. The Storyteller puts 2 Xanadu tokens in the bag. On the 1st night, the player with the good Xanadu token is woken to learn they are the Oracle, and the player with the evil Xanadu token is woken to learn they are the Assassin. Later that night, the Investigator learns that 1 of 2 players is the Assassin, because despite receiving the Xanadu token, that player is still actually the Assassin.
Xanadu is in play. The Storyteller does not put 2 Xanadu tokens in the bag.
The unlisted characters added in by the Xanadu are the Marionette and the Balloonist. During setup, the Storyteller replaces 1 Minion with a Townsfolk, and adds in the Saint, which is listed.

characters.firstNightReminder: Wake the unlisted Townsfolk & inform them of which unlisted Minion is in play. Put them to sleep. Wake the unlisted Minion & inform them of which unlisted Townsfolk is in play. Put them to sleep.

customBoxes.title: The unlisted character tokens
customBoxes.content:
Xanadu ships three tokens: the Fabled token above, plus a good and an evil token for the two unlisted characters it can add.

- **Xanadu (Townsfolk)** — "You are an unlisted Townsfolk." First night 14, other nights 3. Reminders: ?, ?, ?
- **Xanadu (Minion)** — "You are an unlisted Minion." First night 15, other nights 4. Reminders: ?, ?, ?

Both carry the night reminder "Run the unlisted ability accordingly."

characters.name: Dartsman
characters.ability: You start knowing 4 characters, exactly 2 of which are in play.
characters.lede: The Dartsman has pinpoint accuracy, but misses half the time.
examples: The Fugitive and Nurse are in play. The Dartsman learns Nurse, Fugitive, Televangelist & Hypochondriac, only 2 of which are in play.
The drunk Dartsman learns Mystic, Alaphaz, Conspiracist & Bombardier, none of which are in play.

The Hysteria nominates today. Tonight, the Daredevil gains the Dartsman ability and learns Alaphaz, Conspiracist, Nemesis, Tichi. None are in play, but the Hysteria is causing two players to misregister as the Tichi and the Nemesis.
